resale_co.name: Zoning Certificate of Occupancy (ZCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Department of Community Services (Zoning / Code Administration)
resale_co.lead_time: Submit the application at least 10 days before the requested inspection date; the certificate is issued no earlier than 5 business days after the inspection (the form's statement of understanding says 48 hours)
requirements: Sidewalks, curbs and driveway apron in need of replacement must be replaced (Engineering permit)
Permanent house number at least 3 inches high, visible from the street
Roof, fencing, entrance steps, porches and railings in good repair; clear sightline within 10 feet of the curb
48-inch pool fence with self-closing, latching gates
Property cleared of trash, debris and hazardous materials; recreational vehicles or trailers removed or garaged; shrubs and lawn trimmed
Code compliant smoke detectors near each bedroom door and on each level including the basement; sealed 10-year smoke detectors since January 2019
Mounted 2A:10B:C fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, no more than 5 feet above the floor (still on the September 2025 checklist)
Sump pump discharge removed from the sanitary sewer and routed outside
Flue pipes and chimney connections at furnace and water heater sound; water heater and boiler relief valve discharge pipe to within 6 inches of the floor
Handrails 34 to 38 inches high on at least one side of stairs; guardrails on open sides
Working plumbing fixtures, switches and outlets with cover plates; no interior key locks on rooms
Only one kitchen per dwelling; work done without permits must be permitted; zoning violations corrected

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Zoning Certificate of Occupancy Application (all 5 steps, including the new owner's name before the certificate is issued) and submit it with a check payable to 'CITY OF SUMMIT' to the Department of Community Services, 512 Springfield Avenue, at least 10 days before the inspection date. 1-2 family inspections are Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, 9am to 11am; someone 18 or older must let the inspector in. A temporary C/O is issued only for weather or 'as is' sales, and repairs over $200 need an escrow.

evidence.quote: Zoning Certificates of Occupancy (ZCOs) (PDF) are required to be obtained by the Development Regulations Zoning Ordinance for the sale or rental, or for change of occupant or occupancy type for all buildings or for individual units within buildings.
Residential ZCOs must be obtained prior to sale or occupancy of the property.
You may call (908) 273-6407 for questions related to ZCOs or send an email to Karen Kolbeck.
Applications must be submitted ten (10) days prior to the requested inspection date-NO EXCEPTIONS.
A completed C/O will be issued no earlier than 5 business days AFTER the inspection date -NO EXCEPTIONS.
1-& 2-FAMILY DWELLING INSPECTIONS are conducted Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays - 9am-11am
No TCO will be issued when the repair value exceeds $200 unles s an escrow account is established in a manner satisfactory to this office
ONE & TWO FAMILY DWELLING SALE INSPECTION CHECKLIST
Roger Dornbierer Zoning Officer Zoning Officer rdornbierer@cityofsummit.org

resale_co.notes: Summit requires a Zoning Certificate of Occupancy before the sale or rental of every dwelling unit, under the Development Regulations Zoning Ordinance. Fees are from the City's ZCO application (PDF created September 17, 2026). The form also lists $320.00 per unit for a City lead inspection, but only for rentals; rental dwellings built before 1978 need a lead-safe certification. The form has two different issue times: 'no earlier than 5 business days AFTER the inspection date' at the top and 'no earlier than 48 hours AFTER the inspection date' in the statement of understanding. No reinspection fee is listed. The ZCO page names Karen Kolbeck (kkolbeck@cityofsummit.org) for ZCO questions at (908) 273-6407; a 2019 City letter lists her as Secretary for the Department of Community Services. Assistant Zoning Officer: Chris Nicola, cnicola@cityofsummit.org, (908) 273-6407. Rental ZCOs are a separate rental requirement.

requirements: Sealed unit 10-year smoke detectors in all required locations for any residential ZCO for sale or rental since 2019, even if the home has working battery detectors (no change for hardwired AC-powered detectors)
Smoke detectors near each bedroom door and on each level including the basement, not in an unheated attic
Mounted 2A:10B:C fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, no more than 5 feet above the floor (September 2025 checklist)

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA July 2026 registry lists the Summit Fire Department as the fire code enforcing agency (Fire Official Lt. Matthew K. Lemons, (908) 277-9353, mlemons@cityofsummit.org per the state directory), but the Fire Department page says smoke detector certificate inspections for home sales are done by the Department of Community Services, and the state directory also lists 'Summit City Dept Comm Srvcs' for smoke detector compliance. No separate smoke certificate fee was found; the 2019 City letter says the Fire Code smoke requirements are enforced as part of the ZCO process, so the ZCO fee is shown. The Fire Prevention Bureau (908-277-9358) offers free home fire safety inspections. The 2019 letter is a scan read visually.
